title: Combining Conditions
description: Supercharge your decision-making by combining multiple check conditions using logical operators!

content.value: What if you want to go to the park, but ONLY if it is sunny AND you have finished your homework? In Python, we can combine multiple checks using three magical keywords: `and`, `or`, and `not`.
The `and` spell is strict. It requires BOTH sides to be True to output True. If even one side is False, the whole thing is False!

sunny = True
homework_done = True
if sunny and homework_done:
    print("You can go to the park!")
The `or` spell is more relaxed. It only requires ONE of the sides to be True to output True. If both sides are False, only then does it output False!

has_cookie = True
has_cake = False
if has_cookie or has_cake:
    print("You have a sweet treat!")
The `not` spell is like a mirror that flips everything upside down! It turns True into False, and False into True.

raining = False
print(not raining)  # Prints True
